newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suspected militants kill two policemen in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Suspected militants kill two policemen in Egypt.

text.p: Gunmen thought to be Islamist militants killed two policeman in southern Egypt on Saturday, security sources said.

The gunmen shot dead policeman Monsef Khalil Mohamed, 35, outside his house during a wake for a dead relative in the village of Manshiat al-Maghaliqa, in the Nile Valley about 260 km (160 miles) south of Cairo.
A fellow policeman, Adel Ferghali Shalaqami, 41, gave chase and was killed about 20 metres (yards) away before the gunmen escaped into nearby fields, the sources said.
Police suspect the gunmen are members of the Gama'a al- Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest militant organisation fighting the Egyptian government.
Mohamed's brother Mansour, a 38-year-old farmer, was wounded in the first burst of gunfire and was in critical condition in hospital in nearby Mallawi town, the sources said.
The Gama'a has concentrated its attacks on police and suspected informers. It is especially active around Mallawi.
More than 1,000 people, mostly either policemen or suspected militants, have been killed in the political violence in southern Egypt since the Gama'a took up arms in 1992.
